answers.the_problem: Does the litter box's distance from the cat's sleeping/resting area predict in-box vs out-of-box urination for this one cat?
answers.major_literature_families: None formally reviewed -- this is a household case study, not a literature-review-backed claim (see standpoint.disciplines_not_claimed).
answers.closest_constructs: General territorial/resource-placement behavior in domestic cats, as understood from ordinary pet-owner experience, not from a cited behavioral-science construct.
answers.precise_inadequacy: Ordinary household advice ('just clean the box more') does not address distance-to-sleeping-area as a variable at all.
answers.proposed_mechanism: Distance to litter box increases avoidance likelihood, hypothesized as an access-cost effect rather than a substrate or cleanliness effect.
answers.boundary_conditions: Single household, single cat, 14-day window; does not generalize beyond this observed case.
answers.strongest_counterargument: A single cat's preference could reflect an idiosyncratic dislike of that specific box location for reasons unrelated to distance (draft, noise, foot traffic).
answers.strongest_counterexample: If the cat used the box normally on some days at the far distance and avoided it on some days at the near distance, distance would not be the operative variable.
answers.discriminating_empirical_test: A repeated within-subject manipulation of box distance while holding substrate/cleaning constant (see dialogue_table_row.example.json's second observation window).
